title: Governance and security controls are embedded, enforced, and evidenced across every Fabric workload
intro: UHG should establish a common control model across identity, data, connectivity, and workspaces so every workload inherits approved protections while exceptions remain visible and accountable
governance_domains: Application and cloud service role-based access, workload identities, privileged access, and separation-of-duties patterns, integrated with enterprise identity platform services
Standard approval, recertification, revocation, and emergency-access processes

Catalog, lineage, classification, enterprise data quality, MDM, regulatory workflows, privacy and integration controls, ownership, and stewardship integrated with UHG governance and compliance tooling
PHI and sensitive data controls covering encryption, retention, masking, tokenization, and de-identification
Data-product certification and policy requirements carried through downstream consumption and sharing
connectivity_controls: Defined ingress and egress based on workload sensitivity, with outbound
access protection enabled for all workspaces
Workspace, capacity, domain, and environment segmentation to limit
Segmentation patterns aligned to development lifecycle, data classification, and regulatory requirements
Integration with existing SecOps and governance toolsets
Defined exception, escalation, remediation, and continuous-control-monitoring processes
